task: skeptic VALUE+FEASIBILITY check of PC2-13 (L3 lowrefine sensitivity not vacuous; lab forkmid == --patch forkmid; K3 order)
reason: The finding's facts hold, but calling it 'Verified OK, no action' understates it. (1) 44b6_18ced818 has the 'readmitted' flag on 1034 final nodes and kernel stats say 1107: confirmed. Pooled over 56 clips it is 13,284 vs 14,525. (2) The lab forkmid (trainlab.py l.321-352) and the kernel's forkmid_edges (build_probe_kernel.py l.1702-1758) select the same forks. They use the same midpoint formula, scale and victim rule (ILP edge only when edge_prob == 0.0), so they are equivalent; only the audit order differs. (3) forkmid is spliced in as the last edit before the FINAL print, with forkblob after it. I could not re-read the cited scratch build, but forkblob has been CLOSED since 20:05 UTC, so that part of the order no longer matters. What the finding misses: I reran forkmid on all 56 final graphs. 676 forks are eligible, 40 are removed, and 37 touch a readmitted node. Two of the removed forks touch one: 6bba_786893ac (mid 4.681 um) and 6bba_f8ffd5e7 (4.833 um). Two more sit within 0.7 um of 4.5 but are kept: 6bba_969618f6 (4.290) and 6bba_cdcfe533 (4.211). forkmid_v2(lowdet_adverse=True) relabels those rows as removed TP, so removed_tp_eq_0 fails on this lab no matter what the true labels are. Even without the 0.7 um margin, the 2 real removals fail it. So the sensitivity is not just non-vacuous: it decides the result, and ADDENDUM L3 cannot pass. The in-force ORIGINAL T9 forkmid gate has no lowrefine term. If it passes, K3 = K2 + forkmid gets built on a lowrefine stack, even though 2 of the 40 lab removals (5%) involve nodes whose coordinates lowrefine moves. The lab never saw that interaction. Gapfill peaks are also refined by lowrefine but not flagged; I checked, and 0 forkmid rows touch a gapfill-only node, so that gap does not matter here.
fix: Change PC2-13 from 'info, no action' to 'today, before any K3 build'. (a) Write in CONTEXT, before results.md is read, that ADDENDUM L3 is mechanically FAIL on the exp60 lab: its lowrefine sensitivity flags 2 removed plus 2 near-threshold readmitted-touch forks, so asking for the user's OK on L3 cannot open forkmid. The morning OK request should say this, so the user is not asked to approve a gate that cannot pass. (b) If the ORIGINAL T9 forkmid gate passes, add a pre-registered tightening that needs no OK: forkmid in K3 skips a fork when its parent or either child carries the 'readmitted' flag. That removes the 2 lab removals whose geometry lowrefine changes. The lab arm gets rescored with that exclusion, and the original gate must still pass (>= 3 FP removed, >= 1 on 44b6). Alternatively, K3 is built on the no-lowrefine twin (exp58n minus lowrefine) and not on K2. (c) When reporting L3, cite readmitted_nodes_final 13,284 vs kernel_stats 14,525, readmitted_rows_flagged 37, and the 4 adverse rows by stem, as the finding asks.
realistic_gain: No score gain. It is a process safeguard: it avoids spending the user's morning OK on L3, which cannot pass, and it closes a small, unmodelled lowrefine x forkmid interaction (2 of 40 removals, about 0.05 fork per clip) in any K3 built on the in-force original gate. The expected LB and private effect of this is at most +-0.001.
